prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
(empty)

New part:
S001: The Regional Dispatch Center provides continuous intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch, and regional coordination for emergency medical requests across participating jurisdictions.
S002: Its mandate is to translate reported emergencies into prioritized incidents and coordinate an appropriate response under approved clinical and jurisdictional protocols.
S003: The Regional Dispatch Center is known operationally as Juniper and serves as the region’s primary dispatch and coordination point.
S004: The service operates continuously and maintains a shared operational picture of incidents, available units, and known access constraints.
S005: Call Taker Mara obtains essential incident details, confirms the reported location, and enters the request for assessment.
S006: The Triage Supervisor reviews incident information, assigns or confirms priority, and directs cases requiring additional clinical review.
S007: The Regional Medical Director establishes clinical triage policies and defines the limits of protocol-based decision making.
S008: Dispatch personnel apply approved protocols and seek clinical guidance when a case falls outside their delegated authority.
S009: The Shift Commander is the on-duty operational authority for dispatch-center coordination and service continuity.
S010: The Shift Commander is known operationally as Sundial during regional coordination and command communications.
S011: The Shift Commander resolves operational conflicts, sets response priorities during surges, and escalates decisions beyond the center’s authority to the appropriate jurisdictional leadership.
S012: The Shift Commander does not replace the Regional Medical Director’s authority over clinical policy or a Paramedic Crew’s clinical judgment at the scene.
S013: The Radio Coordinator manages operational radio traffic and maintains communications discipline on the Regional Radio Network.
S014: The Regional Radio Network carries dispatch and coordination communications among authorized responders.
S015: The Ambulance Coordination Platform supports a current view of incidents, unit assignments, and regional resource status.
S016: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console is the primary workstation for incident entry, assessment, and dispatch operations.
S017: A Paramedic Crew retains responsibility for immediate patient assessment and care within its professional scope and applicable protocols.
S018: Ambulance Unit 417 is managed as part of the regional response pool when assigned to an incident.
S019: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates operational awareness of receiving capacity and destination constraints.
S020: The Emergency Department communicates receiving considerations through established regional coordination procedures.
S021: Riverside Trauma Center is a designated destination whose availability and suitability are considered under regional protocols.
S022: The North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board provide visible status information relevant to access and movement planning.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
